Admission binds a key to routed address space. An operator announces a /24 over BGP from a live router and answers a signed traceroute probe from three points; the node reads the RIR registry and refuses a claimed prefix, so one ASN issues one seat.

An IPv4 /24 transfers near 10,000 dollars, fees 1,300 yearly, an uplink 400 monthly, so fifty clones run 500,000 dollars plus fifty routers probed every epoch. Rentals still fail the probe. A cedar keeps one crown that reaches the sun, a knoll gathers soil where a slope stops, and an opal claim needs a stake only the claimant can lose.
